title: scandix pecten-veneris subsp. hispanica
intro: Scandix pecten-veneris subsp. hispanica, commonly known as Spanish Scandix or Wild Fennel, is a plant species in the carrot family (Apiaceae). It is used in traditional medicine due to its health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and diuretic properties, making it effective in treating various conditions such as fever, digestive issues, and respiratory problems. The therapeutic actions of Scandix pecten-veneris subsp. hispanica include expectorant, antispasmodic, and antibacterial activities, which help to relieve symptoms and prevent infections. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and are used to treat various health conditions.
